function: Channel estimation: a lightweight residual CNN (LRCNN) with data preprocessing denoises the LS estimate of the direct and cascaded RIS channels from LoRa pilots (p. 3, Sec. III).
system: SIMO uplink: single-antenna LoRa transmitter, K = 8 gateway antennas, passive reflecting RIS (N = 32), LoRa chirp modulation, 125 kHz bandwidth, carrier not stated (pp. 2, 4).
method: Supervised CNN (6 convolutional layers, residual link, Bayesian-optimized hyperparameters), trained with MSE loss and Adam on LS estimates against ground-truth channels, with data preprocessing (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh direct and transmitter-RIS links, Rician RIS-gateway link (10 dB), exponential spatial correlation; 40,000 samples per transmit power, training and validation split 3:1 (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Training/validation 3:1 from the same simulator; power swept -72 to -46 dBm; SF 7, 9, 11 and several RIS sizes shown, with no cross-condition test stated (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Classical: LS and LMMSE; learned: CDRN [8], MRDN [9], DCSaNet [10]; variants: LRCNN without DP, LRCNN with GAM [11] (Figs. 3, 6, pp. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE and BER of coherent LoRa detection with estimated CSI versus transmit power; approximate complexity (Figs. 3-6, Table I, pp. 4-5).
complexity: Table I (p. 5): approximate complexity O(39.5M) for LRCNN versus O(410.6M) CDRN, O(602.3M) MRDN, O(149.6M) DCSaNet, computed according to [19].
openness: Code: https://github.com/gdutsgs/LoRa-RIS-LRCNN (p. 4, footnote 2); the channel data are simulated.
q1_support: p. 4: "modeled as the exponential correlation matrices [18]"; p. 2: Rayleigh direct and transmitter-RIS links, Rician RIS-gateway link. Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, QuaDRiGa or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "The number of samples for each transmit power under different SFs is 40,000, and the ratio between training sets and validation sets is 3:1", so each SF has its own split; p. 5 claims "well-generalized capability for different SFs", but no model trained on one SF or RIS size is stated to be tested on another.
q3_support: p. 5: "Fig. 6 compares the performance of the proposed LRCNN with the existing CDRN [8], MRDN [9], and DCSaNet [10]" (learned, NMSE and BER); p. 4: "achieves better performance compared to the LS and LMMSE estimators" (classical).
q4_support: p. 5: "the approximate complexity of the CNN-based estimators is shown in Table I"; LRCNN O(39.5M) against O(149.6M) to O(602.3M) for the learned baselines.
q5_support: p. 4, footnote 2: "The code is available at https://github.com/gdutsgs/LoRa-RIS-LRCNN."
notes: Included, area 2 with a RIS (SIMO RIS-assisted LoRa, K = 8 antennas and N = 32 passive elements, p. 2). q2 is borderline: Figs. 4-5 vary the SF and the RIS size and p. 5 claims generalization, but each SF has its own 3:1 training/validation split and no cross-condition test is stated, so it is 0; the reviewer should confirm. The learned baselines of Fig. 6 also use the proposed DP (p. 5).
